title: Microsoft Purview: diagnostics that explain DLP and auto-labeling results for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, diagnostic access requirements, controls and licensing background are supported. Minor corrections should complete the shortened role-management route in the guidance and cite the reference establishing the read-only roles' permissions.

claims.claim: The roadmap item is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The general availability target is February CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "February CY2026"

claims.claim: The preview date is January CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "January CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview as release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) only, not US Government clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The change belongs to Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Purview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap names a DLP diagnostic for SharePoint.
claims.quote: DLP SharePoint Diagnostics

claims.claim: The roadmap names a DLP diagnostic for Exchange Online.
claims.quote: DLP EXO Diagnostics

claims.claim: The roadmap names auto-labeling diagnostics for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Auto labeling diagnostics for SPO/ODB

claims.quote: help users understand which sensitive information exist in their document

claims.claim: The roadmap says the diagnostics help explain which labels were applied.
claims.quote: what labels applied

claims.quote: what policies have been triggered

claims.claim: Purview role-group membership is managed through Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: Select Role groups. On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: The control row is correct. In Before rollout, expand the shortened route to 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users', matching the existing row and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to the specified role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: Managing role-group members in the Purview portal requires the Role Management role.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Purview role-group membership grants the roles carried by those groups and is one route to diagnostic permissions.
claims.quote: A role group is a set of roles that enable users to do their jobs across compliance and governance solutions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Entra assignments of applicable diagnostic roles also grant Purview access.
claims.quote: If you assign the Compliance Administrator role in Entra to a user and also assign a scoped Compliance Administrator role in Microsoft Purview, the Entra role overrides the scoped assignment.

claims.claim: The file DLP diagnostic is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Diagnostics.
claims.quote: You can find these diagnostics on the following portal pages: Solutions > Information Protection > Diagnostics; Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Diagnostics

claims.claim: Test-DlpPolicies -workload <workload> -Fileurl <path/direct link> -SendReportTo <smtpaddress> reports which DLP policies match the file.
claims.quote: Test-DlpPolicies -workload <workload> -Fileurl <path/direct link> -SendReportTo <smtpaddress>

claims.claim: The file auto-labeling diagnostic is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Diagnostics.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Diagnostics

claims.claim: Learn links the auto-labeling diagnostic to Test-DlpPolicies, whose own page documents DLP results and the printed -workload, -Fileurl and -SendReportTo call.
claims.quote: Autolabeling isn’t applied to a SharePoint or OneDrive file. Was the file evaluated correctly, and did it meet the autolabeling conditions? ... Test-DlpPolices

claims.claim: Auto-labeling application failures are listed at Purview > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details > Labeling failures.
claims.quote: Select Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select the policy you want to check, and then select View details in the policy details panel. Select Labeling failures to see failed label applications

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -IncludeProgressFeedback retrieves policy labeling progress.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to view. ... Name ... IncludeProgressFeedback specifies whether to include the labeling progress of files in SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The diagnostics are user-opt-in, running on demand when an authorized administrator selects one.
claims.quote: When you select a diagnostic on a Solutions page, the diagnostic runs the Check-PurviewConfig cmdlet to check your organization's configuration settings in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: No separate administrator enablement switch for these Solutions-page diagnostics is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview DLP diagnostics enable disable Check-PurviewConfig admin switch. Read self-help diagnostics, permissions and DLP testing; no switch for these Solutions-page checks. Endpoint always-on diagnostics is a different feature.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft says diagnostics can fix some configuration issues but do not change the tenant without consent.
claims.quote: Although the diagnostics can fix some configuration issues, they don't make changes to your tenant without your consent.

claims.claim: Each Solutions-page diagnostic first runs Check-PurviewConfig to inspect tenant configuration.
claims.quote: When you select a diagnostic on a Solutions page, the diagnostic runs the Check-PurviewConfig cmdlet to check your organization's configuration settings in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: After the configuration check, the diagnostic calls the issue-specific cmdlet listed by Learn.
claims.quote: Then, the diagnostic calls the appropriate cmdlet that's listed in the following table to perform checks that are specific to your issue.

claims.claim: The diagnostics table prints the name Test-DlpPolices for the file checks.
claims.quote: Test-DlpPolices

claims.claim: The SharePoint and OneDrive file checks require a full file path rather than a sharing link.
claims.quote: When entering the file path, make sure that you provide the full file path, not a sharing link.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[1]; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The file DLP check examines properties and classification to explain whether DLP rules matched.
claims.quote: Check a file's properties and classification to review whether a DLP rule matched or didn't match.

claims.claim: The SharePoint and OneDrive auto-labeling check examines properties and classification to determine whether auto-labeling was applied and its conditions were met.
claims.quote: Was the file evaluated correctly, and did it meet the autolabeling conditions? ... Checks a file’s properties and classification to determine whether autolabeling was applied.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; controls[1].note
claims.claim: The Exchange Online check on the DLP diagnostics page accepts an uploaded message trace CSV and reviews DLP rules applied to email.
claims.quote: Upload the message trace log (.csv) to review the DLP rules applied to email messages.

claims.claim: The Outlook on the web policy-tip check analyzes a HAR file exported from browser Developer Tools.
claims.quote: Analyze the HTTP Archive (HAR) file ... Open Outlook on the web, and press F12 to open Developer Tools. Select the Network tab, select Preserve log, reproduce the issue, and export the HAR file.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn describes a gradual Solutions-page rollout that might not yet have reached every organization, despite the roadmap's Launched status.
claims.quote: Diagnostics on Solutions pages are being rolled out gradually and might not yet be available in your organization.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Information Protection diagnostics require Compliance Administrator or Security Administrator.
claims.quote: To run the Information Protection diagnostics, you need to have either of the following roles: Compliance Administrator; Security Administrator

claims.claim: DLP diagnostics accept any of the twelve roles listed in Scope.
claims.quote: To run the DLP diagnostics, you need to have any of the following roles:

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The accepted roles include read-only Security Reader and View-Only DLP Compliance Management, allowing diagnostic access without DLP policy-editing permissions.
claims.quote: Security Reader | View the configuration and reports for Security features. ... View-Only DLP Compliance Management | View the settings and reports for data loss prevention (DLP) policies.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/scc-permissions to sources as 'Roles and role groups in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 and Microsoft Purview'; it documents the read-only permission scopes used in the risk explanation.

claims.claim: Test-DlpPolicies requires a connection to Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: You must be able to connect to Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Test-DlpPolicies emails its report to the SMTP address supplied in -SendReportTo.
claims.quote: The report is sent to the SMTP address specified in the -SendReportTo parameter of the Test-DlpPolicies command.

claims.claim: Test-DlpPolicies works with SharePoint and OneDrive items and reports only policies scoped to SharePoint alone, OneDrive alone or both.
claims.quote: Test-DlpPolicies only works for items that are in SharePoint or OneDrive. Test-DlpPolices only reports results for policies that include SharePoint alone, OneDrive alone, or both SharePoint and OneDrive in their scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The Test-DlpPolicies documentation limits it to simple conditions, excluding complex, grouped and nested conditions.
claims.quote: Test-DlpPolices works only with simple conditions. It doesn't work with complex, grouped, or nested conditions.

claims.claim: IncludeProgressFeedback reports files to be labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: the command shows the progress of files to be labeled

claims.claim: IncludeProgressFeedback reports files labeled in the last seven days.
claims.quote: files labeled in the last 7 days

claims.claim: IncludeProgressFeedback reports total files labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: total files labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy reference documents progress rather than per-file labeling-failure details.
claims.quote: Searched: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy IncludeProgressFeedback file failure details. Read the full cmdlet reference, including all switches and output sections, and the auto-labeling failure article; no per-file failure output is documented for this command.
